report:
## Conclusion

Yes — but with important qualifications. Strong randomized-controlled-trial evidence shows that dexamethasone (and similar corticosteroids) **reduces mortality specifically in patients with severe or critical COVID-19 who require supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation**. The landmark UK RECOVERY trial (>6,000 hospitalized patients) found that a 6 mg daily dose of dexamethasone for up to 10 days reduced 28-day mortality by about one-third in ventilated patients and by about one-fifth in patients receiving oxygen alone (New England Journal of Medicine, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436; RECOVERY Trial results page, https://www.recoverytrial.net/results/dexamethasone-results). This benefit is thought to stem from dexamethasone's ability to dampen the excessive, damaging immune/cytokine response ("cytokine storm") that drives severe lung injury in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

Crucially, the trial also found **no mortality benefit—and possibly harm—in patients who did not need oxygen support**, meaning corticosteroids are not universally beneficial for all COVID-19 cases, only the more severely ill. This nuance was reflected in the World Health Organization's living guideline, which issued a strong recommendation for systemic corticosteroids specifically in severe and critical COVID-19 requiring respiratory support (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/ema-endorses-use-dexamethasone-covid-19-patients-oxygen-or-mechanical-ventilation). Analyses have since estimated the RECOVERY trial's dexamethasone finding saved roughly one million lives worldwide (https://wellcome.org/insights/articles/recovery-game-changing-covid-19-treatment-trial-saved-lives).

**Bottom line:** Dexamethasone-type corticosteroids do improve survival, but only in critically ill, oxygen-dependent COVID-19 patients—not in mild or non-hypoxic cases.
